newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tanker chartering slow, rates steady/firmer.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tanker chartering slow, rates steady/firmer.

text.p: Dirty tanker chartering activity got off to a slow start on Monday but assessments were generally steady to firmer, brokers said.
Business in most regions was slow but the UK/Cont market remained the most active and ongoing demand for tonnage there saw rates holding around last week's firmer levels.
Hound Point to Fawley, and Norway to cont fixings continued to take around W140 with major refiners continuing to provide the bulk of the demand.
Brokers said transatlantic activity remained muted.
Transatlantic activity from the western hemisphere saw a Spanish refiner bringing 70,000 tonnes from Puerto La Cruz but no rate for this fixture was reported.
Mediterranean activity saw good demand for Italy and Spain. 129,000 tonnes from Sidi Kreir to Italy took W82.5 with 80,000 tonne Banias to Spain taking W103.75.
A U.S. refiner booked freight for 50,000 tonnes of vacuum gas oil to the U.S. Atlantic Coast but no rate was reported.
The Middle East Gulf saw moderate VLCC business with tonnage booked to Singapore at a slightly weaker W47 while a voyage to S.Korea to a steady W51.
Fuel oil liftings saw 33,000 tonnes moving Caribs to upcoast U.S. at W162.5 and 50,000 with Atlantic Coast/Gulf options taking W120.
